chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the visitation of the graves,
He said: 'They (the deceased) derive comfort from you, so when you are absent from them, they become scared/lonely.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the deceased when visitors leave the grave?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the dynamic spiritual reciprocity between the living and the deceased in the realm of Barzakh, emphasizing that the souls of the Ahl al-Bayt and righteous martyrs derive comfort from the presence of visitors. It underscores the practical significance of Ziyarah not merely as a ritual for the living, but as a source of spiritual solace and connection for the departed, reinforcing the Shia belief in the continued consciousness and responsiveness of the dead to the faithful.
